description:
Project: “Dedicated throughput SLO + tier definitions” (Dedicated Capacity & Fleet Management)

Goal
- Define clear, enforceable throughput guarantees for Redwood Dedicated customers and translate those guarantees into: (1) hardware shapes (GPU type/count, CPU/RAM, networking), (2) operational policies (admission control, autoscaling/burst rules, maintenance windows), and (3) pricing tiers/contract language.

Problem being solved
- Dedicated customers want predictable capacity, but current commitments are inconsistent across sales proposals, SRE operations, and runtime behavior (batching/scheduling/backpressure). This project aligns product packaging with measurable platform guarantees.

Scope
- In-scope:
  - Formal definition of “throughput” for Dedicated (primary metric + measurement window + exclusions).
  - Tier definitions (e.g., Standard / Performance / Premium) including: minimum sustained tokens/sec (or requests/sec), concurrency assumptions, tail-latency guardrails, and burst policy.
  - Mapping tiers to supported hardware shapes (e.g., L4 vs A100 vs H100 pools, single-node vs multi-node, MIG/no-MIG, NVLink requirements).
  - Observability and reporting: dashboards, customer-visible exportable metrics, internal alerting.
  - Enforcement approach: admission control/backpressure behavior, overload mode, and what happens when SLO is at risk.
  - Pricing/packaging guidance + sales enablement + contract/SLA language.
- Out-of-scope (for this phase):
  - Rewriting the entire Dedicated provisioning pipeline.
  - Per-customer bespoke kernel tuning (handled via separate perf engagements).
  - Full console redesign (only minimal Dedicated tier/SLO surfaced where needed).

Key stakeholders and teams
- Product (Dedicated): Lauren Bishop (DRI), with input from Evelyn Hart.
- Engineering Runtime (scheduling/throughput behavior): Sofia Ivanova, Noah Patel, Omar El‑Sayed.
- Infra Fleet/Capacity: Irene Choi, Vanessa Ortiz, Harish Reddy, Jamal Pierce.
- SRE/SLO governance: Sean Gallagher, Rafael Mendes, Miles Thornton, Aisha Bello.
- Finance/Legal: pricing sensitivity + contract/SLA clauses.
- GTM: Jordan Blake, Stephanie Nguyen, Lukas Meyer (pricing guidance + exceptions process).
- Customer Success/Support: escalation paths when throughput guarantee is missed.

Proposed timeline (6–8 weeks)
1) Discovery + baselining (Week 1–2): workload taxonomy, benchmark runs by shape/model, define measurement standard.
2) Spec + alignment (Week 2–4): PRD + ADRs, tier matrix v1, SRE review for SLO/error budget semantics.
3) Implementation planning (Week 4–6): metrics instrumentation, dashboards, guardrails/admission control hooks, documentation.
4) Launch readiness (Week 6–8): sales enablement, contract language, pilot customers, rollout plan + comms.

Deliverables
- Published Confluence specs: throughput SLO definition, tier definitions, measurement standard, escalation/runbook updates.
- Drive working artifacts: tier matrix sheet, benchmark results, pricing sensitivity model, launch deck draft.
- Linear plan: epics/issues for instrumentation, dashboards, enforcement, comms, and enablement.
- GitHub PRs: metrics + dashboards + guardrails + docs updates.
- Support readiness: Jira templates/playbooks; Slack coordination threads.

Constraints / design considerations
- Throughput varies by model, context length distribution, and streaming behavior; tiers must encode assumptions and exclusions.
- GPU supply volatility: tier availability by region/shape must be explicitly constrained.
- “Guarantee” must be measurable and operationally actionable (alerts, error budgets, mitigation playbooks).
- Avoid incentives that degrade shared reliability (e.g., unbounded bursts) while keeping tiers competitive.

files.description: PRD for Dedicated throughput SLO + tier definitions: customer problem, goals/non-goals, proposed tiers, success metrics, rollout plan, and open questions.
Company-wide measurement standard for throughput: metric definitions (tokens/sec vs req/sec), sampling windows, normalization rules, and exclusions (warmup, maintenance, customer-induced errors).
ADR choosing the primary Dedicated throughput SLO metric (e.g., sustained output tokens/sec at p50/p95) and how it is computed/aggregated per deployment.
ADR defining tier semantics (Standard/Performance/Premium), burst allowances, overload behavior, and what constitutes an SLO breach vs expected throttling.
Published tier definitions: included features, supported shapes, regional availability constraints, throughput guarantees, and operational policies per tier.
Pricing model write-up: how tier pricing maps to fleet costs (GPU/hour, reserved capacity), margin targets, and discount guardrails; includes examples and edge cases.
Catalog of Dedicated hardware shapes (GPU type/count, CPU/RAM, NIC, storage), constraints (MIG/no-MIG), and which tiers each shape supports.
Baseline benchmark results and methodology by shape/model/context-length distribution; used to justify tier thresholds and safety factors.
Formal SLO doc: SLI definition, objectives by tier, error budget policy, alert thresholds, and how violations are tracked and reported.
Dashboards/alerts specification: required panels (throughput by deployment, throttling rate, queue depth, saturation), alert routing, and oncall playbooks.
Escalation playbook for Dedicated throughput complaints: intake checklist, required logs/metrics, triage steps, and when to page SRE/Infra/Runtime.
Runbook for Dedicated overload: immediate mitigations (capacity shift, routing policy change, admission control tuning), verification steps, and comms templates.
Proposed contract/SLA language for throughput guarantees, measurement methodology references, remedies/credits, and carve-outs.
Sales enablement one-pager: how to pitch tiers, qualifying questions, common objections, and rules for discounting/exceptions.
Working notes from kickoff: stakeholders, initial tier ideas, unresolved questions (metric choice, burst semantics), and owners for next steps.
Spreadsheet: tier matrix v1 with throughput targets, concurrency assumptions, supported shapes/regions, and feature toggles (burst, failover, reporting).
Benchmark results sheet: runs by GPU shape/model, notes on variance, and recommended safety factors for guarantees.
Sheet modeling error budget burn under different workload volatility, autoscaling lag, and incident rates; includes alert threshold sensitivity.
Finance model sheet: unit economics by tier/shape, utilization assumptions, and pricing sensitivity ranges; notes for approval review.
Slides draft for internal GTM enablement: new tiers, why now, customer examples, FAQ, and packaging guidance.
Customer comms draft snippets: how to explain throughput SLOs, what telemetry customers get, and how to request capacity changes.
Internal FAQ doc for Support/CS/Sales: definitions, measurement caveats, examples of what is/isn’t an SLO breach, and escalation paths.
Metrics taxonomy draft: naming conventions, dimensions/labels (deployment_id, tier, region, model), and mapping to dashboard panels.
Living decision log: open questions, decisions made, links to ADRs, and follow-up actions.
PM issue to produce PRD + tier proposal; includes acceptance criteria for stakeholder signoff and publish-ready Confluence pages.
PM issue covering pricing updates, guardrails, and coordination with Finance/Legal and Sales enablement.
PM issue to coordinate SLA clause drafts with Legal: definitions, carve-outs, credits, and references to measurement standard.
Engineering issue to add first-class throughput SLI metrics to the runtime/gateway path (export + aggregation rules), with test plan.
Engineering/SRE issue to build dashboards and alerts per Confluence spec; includes rollout and paging hygiene checks.
Engineering issue implementing admission control/backpressure aligned to tier semantics (burst limits, overload mode, throttling).
Engineering issue to represent hardware shapes + tier mapping in configuration/control plane; includes validation and migration plan.
Engineering issue to standardize benchmark workloads used for tier baselines; adds CI/perf-canary coverage.
Support-readiness engineering issue: templates, required data fields, and automation hooks to attach dashboards and logs.
Design issue for minimal console UI: show tier, current throughput vs guarantee, and links to docs/exports.
PR: Add throughput SLI metric emission (per deployment) and standardize labels (tier, model, region); includes unit tests and migration notes.
PR: Implement admission control policy scaffold for Dedicated tiers (burst ceilings, overload mode), gated behind feature flag.
PR: Scheduler instrumentation for queue depth + effective tokens/sec; adds tracing spans for prefill/decode phases.
PR: New Grafana dashboard JSON + alert rules for Dedicated throughput SLO; includes runbook links and default thresholds.
PR: Extend SLO toolkit to support throughput-style SLIs (rate over window) and error budget reporting by tier.
PR: Add perf canary scenario matching tier baseline workloads (prompt length distribution + concurrency), with regression thresholds.
PR: Expose Dedicated tier + shape mapping in Terraform modules and validate unsupported region/shape combos.
Thread coordinating initial tier names/semantics; discussion of tokens/sec vs req/sec and customer expectations; links to draft PRD.
Thread on shape availability by region and supply constraints; proposed restrictions for Premium tier; fleet ops notes.
Thread debating SLO windowing/aggregation and alert thresholds; agreement on error budget policy and paging triggers.

Thread listing required dashboard panels and metric dimensions; questions about tenant isolation and deployment_id cardinality.
Thread requesting a sales-friendly tier cheat sheet and guidance for handling exception asks; PM responses and timeline.
Thread from Support about how to respond to throughput complaints; request for escalation template and dashboards.
Thread announcing internal availability of Dedicated throughput tiers (beta) and where to find docs/dashboards; Q&A replies.
Customer support ticket: Dedicated customer reports sustained throughput below expectation during peak hours; includes initial triage and links to dashboards.
Customer support ticket: questions about what throughput guarantee means for mixed prompt sizes; Support requests official measurement doc.
Internal helpdesk ticket: Sales requests pre-approved language for throughput guarantees in order forms; routed to Product + Legal.
